RADIO SYSTEMS INSPECTION FOLLOWING LIGHTNING STRIKES
1
2
GENERAL
OPERATIONAL CHECK OF RADIO SYSTEMS FOLLOWING A
LIGHTNING STRIKE
INSPECTION OF SYSTEM AFFECTED BY LIGHTNING STRIKE
1. GENERAL
A. The radio installations must be thoroughly checked whenever an aircraft
had had a lightning strike or severe static discharge.
The extent of
the inspection will depend upon the circumstances surrounding the
incident.
B. The flight crew should be de-briefed with regard to the conditions
existing during and after the
"strike". Ref. OD Manual publ. 45.21.10.
If the flight crew ia unavallable, the aircraft log should be read care-
fully to extract whatever information is available.
C.
A visual check from the ground of all antennas, radome, static
dischargers, etc.,
must be made to determine
if any physical damage
has occured.
D. An operational check of all radio Communications and Navigation systems
must be made by a qualified
mechanic or flight crew member, per
Part 2 of this publication. If all radio systems operate normally and
no in-flight malfunctions were reported, no further checks are required.
E. If a radio system mal-function was reported by the flight crew or
detected during the operational check, a detailed inspection of the
affected system or systems must be made per Part 3 of this publication.
F.
After completion of the required checks an entry must be made in the
aireraft log stating that an
"After Lightning Strike" Operational Check
was made, noting any corrective
G.
Any component which has been ren ed from an airereft as & result of a
lightning strike or static discharge must have a Blue Engineering
Evaluation Tag, form 9242-3161 filled out and attached.
H.
If a malfunction exists in a system which is not required for dispatch
of the aircraft Trom a partleular station per Maintenance Manual
publication 1-5-0, repairs may be continued to another statton provided
all safety requirements are satisfied.
